stem: An average-risk client age 30 to 65 chooses cervical cancer screening with high-risk HPV testing plus cervical cytology (co-testing) after counseling. According to current ACOG guidance, which screening interval is acceptable?
rationale: ACOG's 2026 cervical cancer screening guidance states that co-testing with high-risk HPV testing and cervical cytology every 5 years is acceptable for average-risk individuals age 30 to 65 when primary hrHPV testing is not available or, after counseling, the patient chooses co-testing. Therefore C is correct. Annual or 2-year co-testing is more frequent than the recommended interval, and a single lifetime screen is inadequate.
educational_objective: Apply current cervical cancer screening guidance by recognizing a 5-year interval for hrHPV/cytology co-testing in average-risk clients age 30 to 65 when co-testing is selected.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_locator: Summary recommendations/Table 1: co-testing with hrHPV and cervical cytology every 5 years for individuals aged 30–65 years is acceptable when primary hrHPV testing is not available or the patient chooses co-testing after counseling
source_claim_supported: For average-risk individuals age 30–65, hrHPV/cytology co-testing every 5 years is an acceptable screening strategy under the conditions stated by ACOG's 2026 guidance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13: perform targeted screening assessments; educate client about preventive care and health-maintenance recommendations
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — cervical cancer screening / preventive care
correction_summary: Replaced the prior generic rationale that negative co-testing simply provides 'higher confidence' with the current July 2026 ACOG recommendation itself. Specified average-risk age 30–65 and the co-testing choice after counseling, then directly tested the verified 5-year interval. Updated source authority/currentness and exact locator.
audit_findings: C is explicitly supported by ACOG 2026. A and B are more frequent than the stated co-testing interval, while D is not a recommended periodic screening strategy. The stem includes the age/risk/method conditions necessary for the numeric interval to apply, so there is no hidden assumption or second answer. No unsupported precision or unresolved conflict remains.
